engine_gap.source_evidence: wayfinder/SKILL.md: 'Resolving a ticket clears the fog ahead of it, graduating whatever's now specifiable into fresh tickets — one at a time' (Fog of war, L84); 'A session claims a ticket by assigning it... so concurrent sessions skip it' (Tickets, L67); 'the frontier is the open, unblocked, unclaimed children' (Tickets, L69); 'The user may run unblocked tickets in parallel, so expect other sessions to be editing the tracker concurrently' (Invocation, L128).
lower_rungs_attempted: single ordered workflow with a fixed stage list (§6.2/§13.1)
single actor stage whose CONTEXT.md instructs the model to track the ticket graph itself in prose across turns
shared context/helper file describing the convention, executed entirely on the external issue tracker (what wayfinder actually does today)
engine_gap.why_each_fails: Fixed ordered stage list: the resolved WorkflowDefinition is pinned and journaled before execution begins (§3.3, §13.1); wayfinder's ticket set is provably not known at that point -- new tickets are discovered only as prior ones resolve, so there is no fixed stage list to pin. Single actor stage tracking state in prose: a stage's execution is one bounded turn/session per the current engine (§3.4, one backend/one StartRequest per stage); wayfinder explicitly spans many independently-chosen sessions over time, each claiming at most one ticket, with concurrent sessions editing the same durable structure -- this needs cross-session, cross-process durable state, which a single stage's prose cannot hold. Shared-context/helper on the external tracker (today's actual mechanism): this works but places every durable fact -- claim state, blocking graph, frontier, resolution history -- outside Sergeant's own journal entirely, so Sergeant has no evidence of it, cannot recover/resume it, cannot report on it through its own API/TUI/dashboard, and cannot apply its own fail-closed ambiguity handling if two sessions race to claim the same ticket.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: A parent Work whose child checkpoints are not required to be enumerated before the parent starts: the engine can append new child checkpoints as a durable, journaled fact at any point during the parent's lifetime, expose a computed 'frontier' (children with no open blocking child) through its own projections, and support a claim/admission primitive so two callers cannot start the same unclaimed child concurrently -- i.e. real parent/child workflow identity per proposal §7.7's own list of what a hidden pseudo-subworkflow would otherwise lose (parent/child identity, stage-level visibility in the parent, deterministic retry/cancellation, parent-aware recovery, per-subworkflow telemetry, a clear completion contract).
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: Given a Work chartered with zero declared child checkpoints, when an actor stage journals a new child checkpoint mid-run, the engine accepts it without re-pinning or restarting the parent Work, exposes it through the API as an unblocked/blocked child of that parent, refuses a second concurrent claim attempt on the same unclaimed child (observable as a rejected claim, not a silent race), and the parent's own projection (not an external tracker) is sufficient to answer 'which children are currently claimable' after a crash/restart.

statement: Out-of-scope work never belongs in the fog section, because fog only gathers toward the destination; work beyond the destination is recorded in its own Out of scope section instead, and out-of-scope work never later graduates into a ticket unless the destination itself is redrawn as a fresh effort.

source.quote:
Fog only ever gathers _toward_ the destination. The destination fixes the scope, so work beyond it is **out of scope** — it isn't fog, and it doesn't belong in **Not yet specified**. It gets its own **Out of scope** section on the map: work you've consciously ruled out of _this_ effort. Scope, not sharpness, lands it here.

Out-of-scope work never graduates — the frontier stops at the destination — so it returns only if the destination is redrawn, and then as a fresh effort, not a resumption.

trigger: work is identified that lies beyond the chartered destination
outcome: scope creep is recorded explicitly rather than silently absorbed into the fog or the ticket graph
rationale: Deciding whether work belongs in fog or out-of-scope requires judging it against the destination, applied wherever scope questions arise during wayfinder use -- not a mechanical helper check.

statement: When an existing ticket turns out to sit past the destination, close it (making it unambiguously off the frontier) and record one line in the map's Out of scope section gisting why, rather than resolving it as if it were on the route.

source.quote: Ruling something out of scope is a scoping act, not a step on the route. When a ticket that already exists turns out to sit past the destination — mis-scoped in while charting, or exposed by a resolution — **close it** (a closed ticket is unambiguously off the frontier) and leave one line in the **Out of scope** section: the gist plus why it's out of scope, linking the closed ticket. It stays out of **Decisions so far**, which records the route actually walked — a scope boundary isn't a step on

trigger: an existing ticket is found to be out of scope during resolution
outcome: the map accurately distinguishes decisions actually made from work ruled out of scope
rationale: A specific action taken within resolve-ticket once a ticket is judged out of scope (close it, note why) -- requires the judgment call from BU-P4-091 first, so it is stage-context guidance for that stage's flow rather than a standalone mechanical helper.

statement: Never resolve more than one wayfinder ticket per session, except that research tickets may be resolved in bulk (fired in parallel as subagents).

source.quote: Two modes. Either way, **never resolve more than one ticket per session** — with the exception of research tickets.

trigger: a session is working through the map
outcome: each non-research decision gets a session's full, focused attention
rationale: A concurrency-discipline rule (one ticket per session, with a research exception) governing how the resolve-ticket stage is entered each session -- a standing constraint on that stage's own flow, not a deterministic helper step.

statement: Charting a wayfinder map first names the destination via a grilling/domain-modeling session (settling scope first), then maps the frontier breadth-first across the whole space rather than deep on one thread.

source.quote: 1. **Name the destination.** Run a `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` session to pin down what this map is finding its way to — the spec, decision, or change. The destination fixes the scope, so it's settled first.

trigger: a loose, oversized idea is presented to be charted
outcome: the destination is fixed before any tickets are drafted
notes: Cross-references the grilling and domain-modeling skills (P3/P4 partitions) as sub-procedures invoked during charting.
rationale: The charting pass is itself the workflow's first real checkpoint (§6.3): whether implemented as two grilling passes or any other means, 'is the destination fixed and is the frontier mapped' is a durable, observable outcome.
alternatives_considered: stage-context (rejected: whether the destination was fixed before any tickets were drafted is itself the workflow's first observable checkpoint, per its own rationale — not a note nested inside a different stage)

statement: If breadth-first frontier-mapping surfaces no fog at all -- the whole journey is small enough for one session -- stop chartering, do not create a map, and ask the user how they would like to proceed instead.

source.quote: 2. **Map the frontier.** Grill again, **breadth-first** this time: fan out across the whole space rather than deep on any one thread, surfacing the open decisions and the first steps takeable now. **If this surfaces no fog** — the way to the destination is already clear, the whole journey small enough for one session — you don't need a map. Stop and ask the user how they'd like to proceed.

trigger: frontier-mapping during charting surfaces no remaining fog
outcome: a wayfinder map is not created for work that doesn't actually need one
notes: An explicit early-exit branch: charting genuinely completes with 'no map needed' as one of its outcomes.
rationale: An explicit early-exit branch of the chart-map stage with its own observable outcome ('no map needed, ask the user how to proceed') distinct from the stage's normal completion -- a real alternative checkpoint result, not merely guidance folded into the stage's ordinary flow, so it stays a first-class part of the stage's own decision rather than being demoted to stage-context.
alternatives_considered: stage-context (rejected: the no-fog early exit is a distinct, observable outcome of the chart-map stage — 'no map needed, ask the user how they'd like to proceed' — not incidental guidance nested inside another checkpoint)

statement: When creating a wayfinder map, create the tickets that can already be specified as child issues first, then wire their blocking edges in a second pass, because issues need ids before they can reference each other.

source.quote: 4. **Create the tickets you can specify now** as child issues of the map — then wire blocking edges in a **second pass** (issues need ids before they can reference each other). Wiring sorts them into the frontier and the blocked; everything you can't yet specify stays in the fog — the **Not yet specified** section.

trigger: specifiable decisions have been identified during charting
outcome: the resulting ticket set has correct blocking edges despite the two-pass creation order
rationale: A specific two-pass ordering constraint (create issues, then wire edges) that only makes sense as part of chart-map's own ticket-creation flow -- stage-scoped guidance, not a general-purpose mechanical helper reused elsewhere.

statement: After creating research-type tickets during charting, immediately fire a research subagent per ticket in parallel to resolve it, capturing findings on a throwaway branch with a context pointer back to the ticket.

source.quote: 5. **Fire the research subagents.** For each `research` ticket you just created, spin up a `/research` subagent to resolve it in parallel, capturing its findings on a throwaway `research/<name>` branch with a context pointer from the ticket.

trigger: research-type tickets have just been created during charting
outcome: research tickets begin resolving immediately and in parallel, rather than waiting for a future session
notes: Cross-references the research skill (P3 partition); this is exactly the 'shared workflow via ordinary actor delegation' pattern the governing proposal (§7.5-7.6) says is already representable without engine change -- not additional evidence for the engine-gap finding.
rationale: Directs chart-map to delegate research tickets to another skill immediately after creating them -- stage-scoped routing guidance specific to charting, not a standalone deterministic helper action.

statement: When working through an existing map, load only the low-resolution map body (not every ticket's full content), choose the user-named ticket or else the first frontier ticket in order, and claim it by self-assignment before starting any work.

source.locator: Invocation / Work through the map, L122-123
source.quote:
1. Load the **map** — the low-res view, not every ticket body.
2. Choose the ticket. If the user named one, use it. Otherwise take the first frontier ticket in order. **Claim it**: assign it to yourself before any work.

trigger: a session begins working an existing wayfinder map
outcome: exactly one ticket is chosen and claimed before work starts, minimizing map-wide context loaded
rationale: The 'choose and claim' act is the entry checkpoint of the resolve-ticket stage.
alternatives_considered: stage-context (rejected: choosing and claiming a ticket is the resolve-ticket stage's own entry checkpoint with an observable state change — claimed versus unclaimed — not guidance nested inside a different stage)

statement: Recording a wayfinder ticket's resolution means posting the answer as a resolution comment, closing the issue, and appending a one-line context pointer to the map's Decisions-so-far section.

source.locator: Invocation / Work through the map, L125
source.quote: 4. Record the resolution: post the answer as a **resolution comment**, **close** the issue, and **append a context pointer** to the map's Decisions-so-far.

trigger: a ticket's question has been answered
outcome: the map and the ticket both durably reflect the resolution in a fixed three-part sequence
rationale: A fixed three-part sequence for recording a resolution, but tied to the resolve-ticket stage's own completion (it is how that stage ends), not a general-purpose helper invoked from elsewhere, so stage-context rather than helper.

statement: Because unblocked tickets may be worked in parallel by other users, a session working through the map should expect other sessions to be editing the tracker concurrently.

source.locator: Invocation / Work through the map, L128
source.quote: The user may run unblocked tickets in parallel, so expect other sessions to be editing the tracker concurrently.

trigger: a session is working through the map
outcome: the actor's own edits account for the possibility of concurrent external changes
notes: Additional supporting evidence for BU-P4-090's engine-gap finding (concurrent multi-session editing of one shared durable structure).
rationale: A standing expectation the resolve-ticket stage's actor must hold throughout (other sessions may be editing concurrently) -- part of how that stage's actor behaves, not a discrete mechanical helper action, so stage-context rather than helper.
